myth.achil: Achilles in the divine armour Hephaestus made him, leaping forward with his great ash spear, the plain and walls of Troy behind him, his one vulnerable heel just visible.
myth.aegis: Athena's aegis, the goatskin cloak fringed with golden serpents and bearing the Gorgon's head, spread in divine light over a kneeling Greek warrior.
myth.agam: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greek host at Troy, in gold-trimmed armour, raising his ancestral sceptre to rally the army before the ships.
myth.ajax: Ajax the Great, giant of the Greeks, standing guard before the beached Greek ships behind his huge tower shield of seven ox-hides faced with bronze, calm and immovable, watch-fires glowing in the night behind him.
myth.alcinous: King Alcinous of the Phaeacians on his throne in a palace of bronze walls and golden doors, raising a cup in welcome.
myth.altar: A stone altar heaped with votive offerings, small clay figurines, garlands and burning fat, glowing in a dark sanctuary.
myth.ares: The great bronze spear of Ares, god of war, standing upright in scorched earth, smoke and embers swirling around it on a ruined battlefield.
myth.argus: Argus, Odysseus's old hound, lying worn and neglected by the palace gate on Ithaca, lifting his head and wagging his tail as he recognises his master, returned after twenty years disguised as a beggar.
myth.augur: A seer like Calchas reading the flight of birds against a stormy sky, arms raised, the Greek fleet waiting below.
myth.banner: A war standard on a tall pole, a crimson banner snapping in the wind over the Greek camp at Troy, the beached black ships behind.
myth.bastion: Spartan warriors in red cloaks standing shoulder to shoulder as a living wall before unwalled Sparta, because its men were its walls, Mount Taygetus behind.
myth.blackship: The swift black ship of the Phaeacians gliding home over a moonlit sea, the moment before Poseidon turns it to stone.
myth.bow: The great bow of Odysseus that none of the suitors could string, drawn at last in his hall, an arrow flying through the line of twelve axe-heads.
myth.brasidas: Brasidas, the bold Spartan general, leading his men on a night march through the mountains of Thrace, red cloak and crested helmet in moonlight.
myth.breeze: A warm, gentle island breeze sweeping through palms and lotus flowers on a sunlit shore, petals drifting in the air.
myth.brute: A hulking one-eyed Cyclops warrior with a great wooden club, glaring, standing on rocky ground.
myth.bull: A massive sacred bull of Helios with a sun disc glowing between its horns, standing guard over the herd on Thrinacia.
myth.burn: Granaries burning in the night at Ismarus, sparks rising over the fields.
myth.camp: A ragged camp follower in the Greek camp on the beach at Troy, carrying a basket and a water jar between the beached black ships and smoking cook-fires.
myth.canto: The Song of the Sirens made visible as golden ribbons of light flowing over the sea toward Odysseus's ship.
myth.capt: A veteran hoplite captain in a tall horsehair-crested helmet pointing his sword forward, ordering his shield line to advance.
myth.cass: Cassandra, the cursed prophetess of Troy, wild-haired and crying out her warning that no one believes, as the great wooden horse is dragged through the gates behind her.
myth.cave: A shaggy cave beast with glowing eyes lurking in the dark mouth of a cave on the island of the Cyclopes, old bones on the ground.
myth.cbow: A Cicone slinger whirling a leather sling above his head on a rocky hillside.
myth.cdraft: Circe's cup of drugged wine mixed with cheese, barley and honey, a faint green glow rising from it.
myth.cdro: A drowned sailor's pale ghost rising from the dark sea, seaweed in his hair, eyes empty and sad.
myth.ceel: A great eel coiling through the churning waters near Charybdis, sleek and fast.
myth.censer: A bronze censer hanging from chains, pouring out thick, sweet-smelling poppy smoke in a dim island shrine.
myth.cerb: Cerberus, the colossal three-headed hound of Hades, with a serpent for a tail and snakes along his back, snarling with glowing ember eyes at the gates of the underworld, the river Styx and green-black mist behind.
myth.charon: Charon, the grim old ferryman of the dead, poling his boat across the dark river Styx, pale shades waiting on the bank, a coin for the fare in his outstretched hand.
myth.chary: Charybdis, the devouring whirlpool beneath the fig tree on the cliff, sucking down the dark sea into a vast spiral.
myth.chief: The chieftain of Ismarus, a fierce Thracian lord in a fur cloak and bronze helmet, holding a war banner on a hill.
myth.circe: Circe, daughter of Helios, the enchantress of Aeaea, singing at her great loom in her stone hall, a golden wand at her side.
myth.clev: A huge leviathan breaching from the dark sea near the whirlpool, its back like a reef.
myth.clion: A mountain lion of Aeaea, tame and strangely gentle under Circe's spell, prowling in the forest around her palace.
myth.club: The great olive-wood club of the Cyclops lying in his cave, as long as a ship's mast, beside a dying fire.
myth.cmaid: One of Circe's handmaids, a nymph of the springs and groves, carrying a silver bowl of healing herbs.
myth.corsair: A Cicone raider from Thrace leaping from a small boat onto a beach, blade raised, painted shield on his arm.
myth.cow: A sacred cow of Helios, broad-browed with gilded horns, grazing in a golden meadow on the island of Thrinacia.
myth.cscout: A one-eyed Cyclops herder with a heavy stone hammer, standing on a hillside above his flocks on the island of the Cyclopes.
myth.cspa: A small creature of swirling sea foam and spray, shaped like a crouching otter-like beast, rising from a churning patch of dark green sea near a rocky strait.
myth.cup: Circe's golden cup on a stone table in her palace, enchanted drink shimmering inside, pigs in the shadows behind.
myth.curse: A withering curse: a dark, sickly mist curling around a bronze shield and helmet, tarnishing them as it spreads.
myth.cwand: Circe's golden wand glowing with enchantment, a faint swirl of light and a startled pig at her feet.
myth.cwolf: A great grey mountain wolf, enchanted by Circe, fawning gently with its tail wagging outside her stone palace on Aeaea.
myth.dio2: Diomedes the Bold driving his spear at the war god Ares himself with Athena's help, fire blazing from his helmet as the Iliad describes.
myth.dirge: A sorrowful dirge of the deep: Sirens singing on a cliff under a pale moon, a lone bronze bell on a rock, a ghost-grey sea.
myth.doct: A disciplined phalanx seen head-on: rows of round bronze shields locked rim to rim, spears held upright, crested helmets, dust rising around them.
myth.dream: Odysseus's sailors asleep in the long grass of the lotus island, smiling in their dreams, as dreamy mist drifts over them at dusk.
myth.drill: Greek soldiers drilling in formation on a dusty training ground beneath a mountain, a scarred old instructor shouting the time.
myth.drums: Thracian war drums of hide and wood beaten at dawn on a hillside, warriors gathering in the mist behind.
myth.eagle: The great golden eagle of Zeus with a thunderbolt clutched in its talons, wings spread wide against storm clouds.
myth.eel: A huge moray eel lunging from a dark rocky crevice below the Sirens' island, jaws open, in green-blue water.
myth.elder: An ancient grey-bearded Cyclops elder with his single wise, weary eye, leaning on a gnarled staff outside his cave.
myth.eury: Eurylochus, Odysseus's kinsman and second-in-command, a hard bearded sailor-warrior leading the crew ashore on Circe's island with a drawn sword, wary of the forest.
myth.fog: A creeping narcotic fog rolling over the beached black ships of Odysseus, sailors slumped drowsily on the oars.
myth.fury: Ares, god of war, in a crested helmet and wreathed in red fire, gripping a mortal warrior's arm and filling him with sudden battle-rage.
myth.gale: The bag of winds of Aeolus torn open by Odysseus's crew: a howling gale bursts from the leather sack and hurls the ship back across the wine-dark sea, away from the shores of Ithaca.
myth.games: The funeral games for Patroclus at Troy: chariots racing around a turning post, the burial mound behind, crowds of warriors cheering.
myth.garden: The lush Lotus Garden of the Lotus-Eaters, pale lotus flowers and fruit trees under golden afternoon haze.
myth.gate: A guard standing before the Lion Gate of Mycenae, two carved lionesses above the massive stone lintel, his spear barring the way, torchlight on the stone.
myth.gift: A table of gifts of hospitality: a golden cup, a fine cloak, a tripod and bread and wine, set out for a guest in a Greek hall.
myth.hades: Hades, Lord of the Dead, enthroned in the dark underworld with a dark crown and two-pronged staff, Cerberus at his feet, pale shades drifting in the distance.
myth.hammer: Hephaestus, the lame smith god, at his forge inside a volcano, hammer raised over the anvil, sparks and molten light flying.
myth.harrier: A raider blowing a horn from the prow of a ship as a pack of boats rushes into a harbour town at dawn.
myth.hchar: A Trojan charioteer driving two horses at full gallop across the plain of Troy.
myth.hdead: The hungry dead of Hades crowding around a trench of dark offerings, pale and longing, in the grey twilight of Erebus.
myth.heads: Scylla's six heads seen from the deck of a ship, rising from the cliff cave into the mist, each on its long neck.
myth.hearth: The great hearth of Odysseus's hall on Ithaca, the fire burning low; in the shadows Penelope's loom holds the burial shroud she weaves by day and unravels by night.
myth.hecat: A hecatomb, the great sacrifice of a hundred oxen: altar fires burning in a row along the seashore, thick smoke rising to the gods.
myth.hector: Hector, Tamer of Horses and prince of Troy, in gleaming armour with a tall horse-hair crest, standing before the walls of Troy.
myth.helios: Helios the sun god, crowned with rays of light, driving his blazing four-horse chariot across the sky.
myth.herm: Hermes, messenger of the gods, in his winged sandals and winged cap with his herald's staff, flying swiftly over the sea with a message from Olympus.
myth.hgua: An elite Ilian guard in heavy bronze armour with a tall rectangular shield, holding the gate of Troy.
myth.hitr: Cicone horsemen wheeling away into the hills at dawn after striking the Greek camp, dust trailing behind them.
myth.hmil: A Trojan militiaman, an ordinary townsman with a simple shield and spear, standing on the walls of Troy.
myth.honey: A honeyed offering of cakes and a golden bowl of honey left on a sea rock to calm the waters.
myth.hopl: An Argive warrior behind a towering Mycenaean figure-of-eight body shield, wearing a boar's-tusk helmet as Homer describes, braced and immovable on the plain of Troy.
myth.horde: A mounted charge of Amazon warriors across a plain, axes and spears raised, horses at full gallop in a storm of dust.
myth.hspr: A Trojan spearman in a crested helmet before the Scaean Gates of Troy, spear ready.
myth.hurl: Blinded Polyphemus hurling a huge boulder from the cliffs toward Odysseus's escaping ship, a great splash in the sea.
myth.iph: Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, standing calmly at the altar at Aulis in a white robe as the goddess Artemis spirits her away and a deer appears in her place in a burst of light, the becalmed fleet behind.
myth.iris: Iris, goddess of the rainbow and swift messenger of the gods, with golden wings, descending along a rainbow through storm clouds.
myth.isl: A dazed islander of the Lotus-Eaters lying content in tall grass by the shore, a half-eaten lotus fruit in his hand, eyes heavy and dreaming.
myth.javel: A volley of javelins arcing through a dawn sky over a beach where black ships are drawn up.
myth.karma: The three Fates in a dark cave: one spinning the thread of life, one measuring it, one about to cut it with shears.
myth.lamp: Lampetia, the shining nymph, daughter of Helios, herding her father's golden cattle across a sunlit meadow on Thrinacia.
myth.lbow: A Lotus-Eater archer with a reed blowpipe and darts tipped with poppy, crouching among lotus flowers.
myth.leon: Leonidas, King of Sparta, a bearded king in a red cloak and a crested bronze helmet, holding a large round bronze shield, standing calm and proud in a narrow mountain pass at sunset.
myth.lhz: A shimmering golden haze hanging over the island of the Lotus-Eaters, lotus flowers floating in the air, the sea faint and dreamlike.
myth.libation: Odysseus pouring a dark offering into a trench in the ground at the edge of the world, as pale shades gather to drink.
myth.lot: A Lotus-Eater, a lean, smiling man crowned with lotus flowers, holding out the honey-sweet lotus fruit that makes travellers forget their way home.
myth.lure: The Sirens' meadow seen from the sea: flowers and a golden glow luring a ship toward hidden rocks.
myth.lyre: A golden lyre resting on a sea-worn rock, its strings glowing faintly, waves breaking below at twilight.
myth.medic: Machaon, son of Asclepius and surgeon of the Greek army at Troy, binding a wounded warrior's leg inside a lamp-lit tent.
myth.melody: Odysseus bound to the mast of his ship, straining against the ropes as the Sirens' enchanting melody washes over him, his crew rowing with wax in their ears.
myth.mino: The Minotaur, the bull-headed son of the Cretan queen, in the dark stone corridors of the Labyrinth at Knossos, torchlight and bones on the floor.
myth.mourner: A mourning shade, a veiled ghostly woman holding a withered rose, weeping in the gloom of Erebus.
myth.mouth: The mouth of the Cyclops's cave sealed by an enormous boulder, firelight glowing through the gap, sheep pressed inside.
myth.mpill: A Cicone pillager carrying a flaming torch past a burning storehouse at night.
myth.mraid: A Cicone raider of Thrace with a battle axe and a round painted shield, charging out of the dawn mist.
myth.mskirm: A Cicone skirmisher with twin short swords, leaping over a low stone wall in the hills of Ismarus.
myth.muse: A Muse playing a lyre by a spring on Mount Helicon under the stars, a young poet listening, entranced.
myth.nausi: Nausicaa, the Phaeacian princess, by the river mouth where she and her maids washed clothes, turning in surprise as a stranger appears.
myth.navig: A Phaeacian navigator at the stern of a ship that steers itself by thought alone, gazing at the stars above a calm sea.
myth.neith: Phaethusa, the radiant nymph, daughter of Helios, with a shepherd's crook, glowing softly at dawn among the sacred herd.
myth.nike: Nike, the winged goddess of victory, swooping down over a battlefield with a laurel wreath in her hand, her robes whipping in the wind.
myth.nshade: A dark, glinting draught of nightshade in a small clay vessel, purple nightshade berries and leaves around it, faint violet vapour.
myth.oarsman: A Phaeacian oarsman pulling at the oar of a swift, sleek ship on a calm sea, the island of Scheria behind.
myth.ossuary: The inside of a beehive tomb like the Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae: bones, bronze helmets and grave gifts laid in the dark, a single shaft of light from the doorway.
myth.owl: The little owl of Athena with wide golden eyes, gliding on silent wings over the moonlit Acropolis.
myth.ox: A white ox with gilded horns and a garland of flowers being led to the altar for sacrifice, as in the Homeric rites, smoke and a priest waiting.
myth.pegasus: Pegasus, the winged white horse born from the blood of Medusa, rearing in flight above the clouds at dawn.
myth.peltast: A light-armed Greek skirmisher with a crescent-shaped wicker shield, running and hurling a javelin.
myth.pent: Penthesilea, queen of the Amazons, charging into battle at Troy on horseback with a double-headed axe and a crescent shield.
myth.phguard: A guard of Scheria in polished bronze, standing before the gleaming golden gates of King Alcinous's palace.
myth.pikeman: A guard of the Taphians, the sea-raiding people of the Odyssey, with a long pike and a hide shield, standing watch over a rocky harbour.
myth.pit: A dark pit at the edge of the underworld, pale ghostly hands and faces rising from its depths in the mist.
myth.plunder: Raiders carrying golden vessels and a bronze tripod out of a burning temple at night, the cult statue watching from the flames.
myth.poly: Polyphemus the Cyclops, son of Poseidon, the giant one-eyed shepherd standing at the mouth of his cave with a whole tree for a staff.
myth.priam: King Priam of Troy, a white-bearded old king in royal robes, looking out from the walls of his city.
myth.priest: A Poppy Priest of the Lotus-Eaters in a robe of red poppies, swinging a smoking censer, sweet drowsy smoke curling around him.
myth.pyre: A towering funeral pyre burning on the beach at Troy at night, like the pyre of Patroclus, sparks spiralling up to the stars.
myth.pythia: The Pythia, the oracle of Delphi, seated on a bronze tripod in the dark inner temple, entranced, holding a laurel sprig as vapours rise around her.
myth.rally: A herald on a hilltop blowing a war horn as the scattered Greek warriors below rise and turn back toward the fight.
myth.ram: Warriors under a wooden roof swinging a bronze-headed battering ram against a great city gate, splinters flying.
myth.rampart: The towering walls of Troy, which the myths say Poseidon and Apollo built, seen from below at dusk, torches burning along the battlements.
myth.reaper: A tall plant creature of woven lotus stems and drooping poppy heads, holding a crescent sickle, standing in a misty field of sleep.
myth.reaver: A hooded assassin in shadow dipping arrowheads into poison from a small clay pot, like the arrow-poison Odysseus sought at Ephyra.
myth.requiem: Mourners lamenting over a fallen warrior laid on a bier, arms raised in grief as on ancient Greek funeral vases, torches against a dark sky.
myth.sack: Odysseus's men sacking and burning Ismarus, city of the Cicones, at night, the first raid on the voyage home from Troy.
myth.sacril: The angry sun god Helios glaring down from his blazing chariot onto the island of Thrinacia, the sacred herd below.
myth.sailor: A sailor of Odysseus's fleet straining at the oar of a black-hulled Greek ship with painted eyes on its prow, spray flying, the wine-dark sea at dusk.
myth.sails: The white sails of a Phaeacian ship filled with a favouring wind, racing over a bright sea.
myth.salve: Asclepius, the god of healing, with his staff entwined by a single serpent, gently applying a salve to a wounded warrior's arm.
myth.sapper: A Trojan saboteur creeping through the night with a torch and a pick, undermining the wooden palisade of the Greek camp.
myth.scorch: A blinding ray of sunlight scorching down from the sky onto a rocky shore, the air shimmering with heat.
myth.scout: A small Siren as the Greeks painted her, a woman's head on a bird's body, perched on a sea rock, watching for passing ships.
myth.scyl: Scylla, the six-headed monster of the strait, her six heads on long necks rising from her cave high in a sea cliff above a passing ship.
myth.sent: An Argive sentinel on night watch on the earthen wall the Greeks built to guard their ships at Troy, a tall shield planted beside him, watch-fires behind.
myth.sh1: One of Scylla's six heads on a long snake-like neck snapping out from a sea cave, rows of teeth bared.
myth.sh2: A gnashing head of Scylla on a long neck, emerging from the mist of her cliff cave, teeth bared.
myth.sh3: A head of Scylla that bays like a hound, its long neck stretched out from the cave, mouth open in a howl.
myth.sh4: A green, venomous head of Scylla on a long sinuous neck, dripping venom, lunging from the dark cave.
myth.shade1: A restless shade of the dead, a pale translucent figure drifting in grey mist at the edge of the underworld.
myth.sheep: A fat, woolly ram from the flock of Polyphemus standing in the Cyclops's cave, the kind Odysseus clung beneath to escape.
myth.shield: The Shield of Achilles that the smith god Hephaestus forged, its bronze face worked in rings showing earth, sea, sky, cities at peace and at war, glowing on the anvil of his forge.
myth.shoal: Jagged rocks just beneath the surface of a dark sea, foam breaking over them, a ship's broken oar caught among them.
myth.sip: A hand offering a clay cup of honeyed lotus drink, sweet golden vapour rising from it, on a sunlit island shore.
myth.siren: A Siren of Anthemoessa, the flowery island of the Sirens: a bird-woman with great wings spread, singing among flowers above the sea, Odysseus's ship far below.
myth.skies: A chorus of Sirens circling in a stormy twilight sky above the sea, wings wide, singing together.
myth.song: A Siren with a woman's face and a bird's wings and body, singing from a rock in the sea, her song rippling visibly through the air.
myth.spear: A seasoned Ithacan spearman, a grown soldier in a simple bronze helmet and linen cuirass, braced behind a round bronze shield, spear levelled, on the rocky shore of Ithaca with a dark sea behind him at dusk.
myth.spearc: A bronze-tipped spear hurled across the plain of Troy in a duel before the city walls, caught mid-flight, dust and a blood-red setting sun behind it.
myth.sphinx: The Sphinx of Thebes, with a woman's face, a lion's body and an eagle's wings, perched on a rock outside the city to pose her riddle, bones scattered below.
myth.spoils: A heap of plunder on a beach beside a black ship: bronze tripods, golden cups, captured armour and shields, glinting in torchlight.
myth.tbull: The great white bull that Poseidon sent from the sea to King Minos, rising out of the waves onto the shore of Crete.
myth.telem: Telemachus, the grown son of Odysseus, standing at the prow of a ship leaving Ithaca to seek news of his father, the goddess Athena beside him disguised as old Mentor.
myth.testudo: Warriors crouched under a locked roof of shields as a rain of arrows and stones falls on them from a city wall.
myth.thanat: Thanatos, the winged god of death, a solemn dark-winged young man holding an upside-down extinguished torch, gliding silently over a battlefield at dusk.
myth.thermo: The narrow pass of Thermopylae between cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek shields facing an endless Persian host at sunset.
myth.thess: A Thessalian horseman galloping across the plains of Thessaly, cloak streaming, javelin raised, a storm sky over the mountains behind.
myth.thunder: Zeus hurling a jagged thunderbolt from the storm clouds, striking Odysseus's ship at sea as punishment for eating the sacred cattle of Helios.
myth.tide: A gentle, glowing tide washing over a wounded warrior lying on a sunlit beach, healing light in the water.
myth.titan: A colossal stone giant asleep on the island of the Lotus-Eaters, overgrown with lotus vines, one heavy eye half open.
myth.trident: The trident of Poseidon rising from a stormy sea, crackling with power, waves rearing around it.
myth.undertow: A powerful undertow dragging a ship's anchor and rope down into the dark, swirling water.
myth.veteran: A grey-bearded Athenian hoplite with old scars, standing on the marshy plain of Marathon, the burial mound of the fallen behind him.
myth.wall: A wall of round aspis shields painted with bold emblems (a scorpion, a Gorgon's face, a charging bull), locked together, seen close up.
myth.walls: The great walls of Troy rising over the plain at sunset, the Scaean Gates shut tight.
myth.warden: A warden of the dead in dark bronze armour, standing guard before the gates of Erebus with a long spear.
myth.whirl: The whirlpool Charybdis seen from above, a vast spiral of dark sea, a ship's timbers caught at its rim.
myth.zerk: A frenzied warrior possessed by Ares, eyes wild, mouth open in a war cry, charging, while the war god's red shadow looms behind him in the smoke.
myth.zeus: A white marble altar of Zeus on a mountain-top at night, offering smoke rising from it, a crackling bolt of lightning striking down onto the altar from a storm-black sky.
